U.S. News Announces 2026 Best Colleges Rankings Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation

The 41st edition serves as a year-over-year benchmark for students and families.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 23, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- U.S. News & World Report, the global authority in education rankings, today announced the 2026 Best Colleges rankings.

Serving as a guide for prospective students and their families, the national and regional rankings evaluate nearly 1,700 colleges and universities using up to 17 measures of academic quality. In a show of continued excellence, eight of the top-ranked schools in the ten ranking categories retained their No. 1 position, with the remaining two finishing a strong second.

"For over four decades, Best Colleges has served as a trusted and data-backed resource for students and families navigating the complex college search process," says LaMont Jones, Ed.D., managing editor for Education at U.S. News. "Over the years, Best Colleges has evolved into a comprehensive tool that reflects the changing landscape of higher education, providing prospective students with a crucial starting point to identify schools that align with their academic and personal goals."

Core methodology and weighting factors remained the same this year, but small portions of underlying data were adjusted to reflect evolving admissions considerations, cohort representation and student involvement.

"While the general scoring weights and factors remained consistent, the 2026 rankings made a few small adjustments to ensure the results accurately reflect the evolving landscape of higher education," says Jones. "By considering students' credit hours and increasing the minimum number of students for a cohort, the rankings deliver a view of institutional investment in students, and graduation and retention rates."

This edition of the rankings also includes specialized rankings, such as the best value schools, most innovative colleges, top performers on social mobility and historically Black colleges and universities, as well as universities with the greatest commitment to undergraduate teaching. Additionally, students can find Programs That Enhance Student Experience, including first-year experiences, co-ops/internships, service learning, study abroad and undergraduate research/creative projects.

Supporting the rankings, U.S. News publishes content related to college affordability. This year, advice includes topics such as " See the Average College Tuition in 2025-2026," " 8 Types of Part-Time Jobs That Pay for College," and " 10 Most and 10 Least Expensive Private Colleges."

The 2026 Best Colleges methodology is calculated using up to 17 key measures of academic quality for National Universities and 13 indicators for the National Liberal Arts Colleges, Regional Universities and Regional Colleges. The formula uses data universally reported by schools or obtainable from third-party sources. Schools' eligibility to be ranked is not contingent on participation in U.S. News' surveys. Institutions and media wishing to learn more about this year's updates to the ranking methodologies can register for our upcoming webinar on October 9.

The annual college rankings from the U.S. News& World Report have been released, showing few major change among the country’s top schools for 2026.

The top three spots remain unchanged, with Princeton University in New Jersey topping the list.

## Why It Matters

College rankings are influential tools for prospective students and their families.

#### Read More on U.S.

While the usefulness of college rankings is often debated, with the practice being seen as somewhat subjective or imperfect, U.S. News rankings continue to play a major role in shaping college admissions and influencing institutional prestige.

## What To Know

The 2026 ranking from U.S. News shows Princeton University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Harvard University retaining their top three spots.

Yale and Stanford tie for fourth place in the ranking, with Yale having risen from fifth place last year.

...

The University of California, Berkeley, overtook UCLA to become the top-ranked public university, ranking 15 and 17 respectively on the list.

Williams College has been named the top national liberal arts college, while Spelman College tops the list of historically Black colleges, both retaining their spots from last year.

Only a handful of schools—the University of Chicago, the California Institute of Technology and Northeastern University—moved five or more spots compared with last year’s ranking.

The University of Chicago rose to number six from 11 last year. Caltech switched places with it, falling from six to 11.

U.S. News & World Report ranks more than 1,700 colleges using a weighted formula that considers factors such as graduation and retention rates, faculty resources, academic reputation, financial resources and student selectivity.

The publisher said it made only minor adjustments to its methodology this year, following substantial changes last year that caused significant shifts in the rankings, particularly boosting several public universities.

## What People Are Saying

LaMont Jones, Ed.D., managing editor for education at U.S. News, said in a press release: "For over four decades, Best Colleges has served as a trusted and data-backed resource for students and families navigating the complex college search process."

"Over the years, Best Colleges has evolved into a comprehensive tool that reflects the changing landscape of higher education, providing prospective students with a crucial starting point to identify schools that align with their academic and personal goals."

## What Happens Next

The top-ranked schools will likely highlight their standings to attract applicants and donors, and prospective students and families may use the rankings as a reference.

# US News HE rankings 2025: Princeton, MIT and Harvard hold top spots as Berkeley overtakes UCLA as leading public university

Share

AA

+Text Size

- Small
- Medium
- Large

The 2025 US News HE rankings reveal Princeton, MIT and Harvard holding top national spots, with the University of California, Berkeley overtaking UCLA as the leading public university. Despite a turbulent year for US higher education, the rankings show minimal change. Minor formula tweaks were made, and only a few universities shifted significantly in the top 50. The report remains influential amid ongoing debates about ranking methodologies and their role in admissions.

U.S. News Releases 2025 HE Rankings After Year of Sector Cuts, Controversies and Change. (AI Image)

The 2025 US News & World Report higher education (HE) rankings have been released, revealing little change at the very top despite a year marked by significant challenges for American colleges and universities. Princeton University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), and Harvard University have maintained their positions as the top three national universities. Meanwhile, the University of California, Berkeley, has surpassed UCLA to become the highest-ranked public university.Across the country, higher education institutions have faced funding cuts, demographic shifts threatening enrolment, and increased pressure from the White House under President Trump. Yet, the U.S. News rankings, a key reference for many parents and prospective students during admissions season, show a remarkable degree of stability.Top universities show little movement despite sector challengesAfter a turbulent year for the HE sector, the annual rankings published by U.S. News reveal that the traditional hierarchy remains largely intact. Stanford University retains its fourth position, now tied with Yale University, while Williams College continues to be rated the best national liberal arts college.

Historically Black institutions see Spelman College once again recognised as the top school in that category.Berkeley’s rise to lead the public university rankings marks the only significant positional change at the top, swapping places with UCLA. This switch highlights regional dynamics within the University of California system, which remains highly influential in the public university landscape.Despite some criticism, US News continues to assert the importance of its rankings as a consumer guide for one of life’s most significant purchases. The publisher claims its education website attracts at least 100 million visitors annually, even after ceasing its print edition in 2010.Changes in methodology and leadershipUS News confirmed that the 2025 rankings include only minor tweaks to their formula, designed to better reflect current admissions practices and student engagement. The report dismissed suggestions that political turmoil or White House interventions influenced these adjustments.Notably, Robert Morse, who has been involved with the rankings since their inception in 1983 and led the programme since 1989, retired earlier this year. This transition raised questions about potential methodological shifts, but the publisher maintains that core elements remain consistent.Noteworthy movements in the top 50While the top positions showed limited shifts, a few universities experienced significant changes. Northeastern University climbed eight spots to share 46th place, while the University of Chicago rose to sixth, displacing the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), which dropped to 11th. Caltech did not respond to requests for comment on its fall in ranking.Only three national universities moved at least five places in the top 50, indicating a generally stable landscape that contrasts with the upheaval seen in previous years when methodology changes caused dramatic reshuffling.US News rankings and the broader landscapeIt is important to note that U.S. News is not the sole arbiter of college rankings. Other publications, such as Washington Monthly, offer different perspectives. For example, Washington Monthly ranked Berea College as the best institution for value in terms of tuition and tax dollars, placing Princeton fifth and Harvard 28th on its list. U.S. News ranked Berea tied for 45th among liberal arts colleges.According to Richard K. Lyons, Berkeley’s chancellor, quoted by The New York Times, while he acknowledges the university’s strong reputation, he cautions against placing too much emphasis on any single ranking system, given their varied weighting methods. He stated, "For users, I’d say take weighted averages. But to presidents, you’ve got to stand on your values first," as reported by The New York Times.Selected rankings of top universities in U.S. News HE rankings 2025

The annual U.S. News rankings remain a key benchmark for the U.S. HE sector, despite ongoing debates about their methodology and impact. As colleges prepare for the upcoming admissions cycle, the rankings continue to influence decisions by students, families, and administrators alike.
